key_insight: At high Reynolds number, moderate adverse pressure gradients mainly add an outer, wall-incoherent shear-layer-like energy component, while the wall-scaled attached-eddy hierarchy remains largely unchanged and coherent with the wall.
engineering_relevance: This helps predict when boundary-layer models must account for outer-layer energisation and altered stress distributions in pressure-gradient flows relevant to turbomachinery, aerodynamics, and flow control.
method: Matched high-Reynolds-number ZPG and APG boundary layers with minimal upstream pressure-gradient history.
Used a two-point hot-wire setup to estimate the linear coherence spectrum and separate wall-coherent from wall-incoherent energy.
Applied conditional averaging to PIV data to identify the structures behind outer-region energisation.
evidence_signal: Two complementary datasets at friction Reynolds number around 10,000 show that extra APG energy is mostly incoherent with the wall and increasingly penetrates the logarithmic region as pressure-gradient strength grows.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on specific moderate APG cases at matched high Reynolds number, so extrapolation to stronger gradients or different histories should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Wall-scaled eddies and embedded shear layers in high-Reynolds-number moderate adverse-pressure-gradient boundary layers
